question: According to the Spaulding classification, which level of disinfection is required for a flexible endoscope used for upper GI endoscopy (a semi-critical device)?

answers.text: High-level disinfection (e.g., glutaraldehyde 2% for 20–30 minutes), which kills all organisms except high numbers of bacterial spores

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Semi-critical items (those contacting intact mucous membranes but not sterile tissue) require high-level disinfection. Glutaraldehyde 2% (Cidex) for 20–30 min achieves this; it kills vegetative bacteria, mycobacteria, most fungi, and viruses but not necessarily all spores.

answers.text: Sterilisation (e.g., autoclaving at 121°C), which destroys all microbial life including spores

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Sterilisation is required for critical devices (those entering sterile tissues, e.g., surgical instruments). Flexible endoscopes cannot withstand autoclaving — they require high-level disinfection.

answers.text: Low-level disinfection (e.g., quaternary ammonium compounds), which kills most vegetative bacteria and some viruses

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Low-level disinfection is for non-critical items (environmental surfaces, blood pressure cuffs). It is insufficient for semi-critical devices like endoscopes.

answers.text: Antiseptic application (e.g., povidone-iodine) on the endoscope surface before insertion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Antiseptics are formulated for use on living tissue, not for reprocessing reusable medical devices. Using povidone-iodine on an endoscope instead of high-level disinfection would be a serious infection control failure.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Classification and Principles blocks. The Spaulding classification: critical items → sterilisation; semi-critical (contact with mucous membranes) → high-level disinfection; non-critical (contact with intact skin) → low-level disinfection.

Well done. The Spaulding framework (critical → sterilisation; semi-critical → high-level disinfection; non-critical → low/intermediate-level disinfection) is the foundation of infection control decision-making.
